correctness.rationale: The batch force equals c times an orthogonal block-contrast projector. Its permutation-averaged square yields the exact two-mode mean-square factor rho and the sharp h_max. Synchronous coupling proves existence/uniqueness with finite second moment; the stationary covariance solves two scalar Lyapunov identities. At h_* every update is a scalar orthogonal reflection, so the Gaussian mixture collapses. Outside h_* the conditional variance of an e1-e2 contrast depends on whether particles 1 and 2 share a batch, yielding the displayed strict fourth-moment lower bound by conditional Jensen. The finite exact-rational checker enumerates partitions to verify critical projector and pair-probability identities; it is not treated as a proof of all N.

value.rationale: A harmonic all-to-all particle system has an exactly Gaussian continuous-time target, making distributional Gaussianity a natural and important benchmark for randomized Gibbs sampling. The theorem shows that unmodified random batching generically destroys Gaussian shape even with Gaussian external noise, pinpoints one unexpected reflection-step exception, and quantitatively certifies non-Gaussianity for every N and proper batch size via an explicit fourth-moment defect. It distinguishes Gaussianity from target correctness and supplies a sharp stability ceiling, not just a small finite example.
